source.documentTitle: General Retail Industry Award 2020 [MA000004], Fair Work Commission consolidated modern award

notes: Retail Employee Levels 1 to 8, full-time, part-time and casual, adult and junior (cl. 17.1, 17.2).
Shiftwork other than baking production (cl. 24.1, 25.1). Baking production employees (cl. 24.2, 25.2) are not modelled.
Apprentices, trainees and the supported wage system (cl. 17.3 to 17.7) are not modelled.
Full-time and casual employees working to an averaging roster (cl. 15.6(g), 21.2 Table 10) need review: weekly overtime is calculated on a one-week basis only.
Higher duties (cl. 17.5), recall (cl. 19.11) and travelling time (cl. 19.5) are not modelled. Reimbursements depend on actual costs and are not calculated.
Enterprise agreements replace the award and are not modelled.

sources.excerpt: (a) Any shiftwork between midnight Sunday and midnight Friday must be paid at the rate of 130% of the minimum hourly rate for full-time and part-time employees and at 155% of the minimum hourly rate for casual employees (inclusive of the casual loading).

sources.excerpt: (c) Any shiftwork on a Sunday must be paid at the rate of 175% of the minimum hourly rate for full-time and part-time employees and at 200% of the minimum hourly rate for casual employees, inclusive of the casual loading.

rateRules.description: Work before a 12-hour break between work days

sources.excerpt: If an employee starts work again without having had 12 hours off work, the employer must pay the employee for each hour worked at the rate of 200% of the employee’s minimum hourly rate until the employee has a break of 12 consecutive hours.
An employer must pay a casual employee for each hour worked a loading of 25% on top of the minimum hourly rate otherwise applicable under clause 17—Minimum rates.

verification.notes: Full-time and part-time: 200% as stated in cl. 16.6(b). Casual: the award states no casual figure, so 225% is derived by adding the 25% loading of cl. 11.1, the same way Table 11 Note 2 derives every casual overtime rate. A public holiday or overtime rate applies instead when it is higher.

casualWeeklyOrdinary.description: Casual overtime threshold: hours in excess of 38 ordinary hours per week (or averaged over a roster cycle).

sources.excerpt: Casual employee | Overtime is payable for hours worked: (i) in excess of 38 ordinary hours per week or, if the casual employee works in accordance with a roster, in excess of 38 ordinary hours per week averaged over the course of the roster cycle; or (ii) outside the span of ordinary hours (excluding shiftwork), subject to clause 15.2; or (iii) in excess of 11 hours on one day of the week and in excess of 9 hours on any other day of the week.

minimumBreakBetweenWorkDays.description: Minimum break between finishing work on one day and starting on the next (10 hours by agreement under cl. 16.6(d)).

sources.excerpt: An employee must have a minimum break of 12 hours between when the employee finishes work on one day and starts work on the next.

If an employee starts work again without having had 12 hours off work, the employer must pay the employee for each hour worked at the rate of 200% of the employee’s minimum hourly rate until the employee has a break of 12 consecutive hours.

verification.notes: The award gives the junior percentages but not the rounding. Taking the percentage of the full-time weekly rate, dividing by 38 and rounding half-up to the cent, then applying each penalty or overtime percentage to that rounded rate, reproduces all 754 junior and adult rates published in Schedule B.1 to B.3 (checked by test).

roundingPolicy.rationale: The award does not prescribe a rounding method. Each hourly rate is rounded to cents half-up: adult rates from the Table 4 hourly rate, junior rates from the weekly rate times the junior percentage divided by 38. That reproduces every rate published in Schedule B.1 to B.3. Each pay line (rate × hours for one rule and rate over the pay period) is then rounded once to cents, half-up. Employers may round at other stages, so reconciliation applies an explicit rounding tolerance.
